concerns.text: The plan proposes generating 'synthetic NDVI time-series (random walk with seasonal component)' to validate statistical logic. A random walk with seasonality does not replicate the spatial autocorrelation, crop phenology, or noise structure of real Sentinel-2 data. Consequently, the VIF diagnostics, robust standard errors, and sensitivity analysis (cloud cover sweep) will not reflect the true statistical properties of the intended data, rendering the 'structural validity' claim methodologically unsound for the specific regression models proposed.

The mitigation strategy relies on a 'csabstruct' HuggingFace dataset as a proxy for LSMS-ISA. This dataset is described as 'Text-only' or 'Structured data on CSA practices' without explicit confirmation of geospatial coordinates, household-level financial access, or HFIAS scores. If the proxy lacks the specific confounders (Finance) or outcomes (HFIAS) required by the regression models, the analysis cannot be performed. The plan treats this as a 'structural' test, but without the actual variable distribution, the regression coefficients and p-values generated are mathematically arbitrary and cannot validate the methodology's ability to detect the hypothesized effect.

The study design targets N > 1000 households but relies on a spatial join between fuzzed household coordinates and satellite pixels. In observational studies with fuzzed coordinates (privacy protection), the linkage rate often drops significantly below 95% (SC-001 target) due to the 'fuzzing radius' exceeding the pixel resolution or the uncertainty of the true location. The plan does not account for the statistical power loss if the effective N drops below the threshold required to detect the effect size, nor does it define a minimum viable N for the village-level aggregation fallback to remain statistically meaningful.
